VERIFIED_TERMINATION.definition: Provider asset status = inactive AND historical bars stop AND no mapped successor continues (e.g., via asof rename chain). Strong evidence of delisting/merger.

RENAMED_SUCCESSOR.definition: Bars stop under ticker but provider asof mapping links successor entity (e.g., FB->META). Valid from/to defined by rename date, bars assigned to ONE entity, no duplicate same-date bars across aliases.

POSSIBLE_DELISTING.definition: Inactive + bars terminate but no direct event metadata (no rename link). Inferred from status + bar termination coherence.
POSSIBLE_DELISTING.example: Inactive OTC with last bar 2019-03-15, tradable false

DATA_GAP.definition: Active asset but history unexpectedly terminates before dataset end or has severe gaps (>20% missing vs expected trading days). Not termination, likely data outage or feed limitation.
DATA_GAP.example: Active NASDAQ with last bar 2024-01-10 but expected 2026-07-30

UNKNOWN.definition: Ambiguous: insufficient data, conflicting status, or short history (<63 bars). Do NOT convert UNKNOWN directly into delisting event.

TIER_A_VERIFIED_PIT.definition: Historical existence/termination supported by strong provider evidence (active/inactive status + asof mapping + bar continuity). Highest confidence.
criteria: bars continuous through rename where applicable
TIER_A_VERIFIED_PIT.expected_count: To be determined after full probe

TIER_B_RECONSTRUCTED_PIT.definition: Historical lifetime inferred from inactive status + historical bars + rename mapping with coherent evidence but no exact official listing/delisting event.

TIER_C_APPROXIMATE.definition: Only bar-presence based lifetime is available (first/last observed bar). No status or rename mapping support.
criteria: may include survivors with late entry

TIER_D_UNUSABLE.definition: Ambiguous identity, severe gaps, invalid mapping, insufficient data (<63 bars or >20% missing).

current_dataset_mapping.note: Current dataset's 1193/1194 survivors would be classified as TIER_C_APPROXIMATE at best, since no provider evidence for termination was used. This is why it is survivorship-biased.
